title: Cross-provider evaluation migration workflow
summary: Use this playbook to move an existing evaluation between providers while preserving its test intent, comparison evidence, and decision criteria. It also identifies when differences prevent a valid comparison.
prerequisites: An existing evaluation with representative test cases and recorded results
A documented scoring method and acceptance criteria
Authorized access to the source and destination providers

sections.title: Answer and source update
paragraphs: How do you migrate an evaluation without mistaking implementation differences for model-quality differences? Preserve the evaluation's test cases, instructions, scoring rules, acceptance criteria, and evidence; document every provider-specific adaptation; then compare results only after checking that the two runs measured the same intended behavior. This is an intermediate-level playbook for practitioners who already have an evaluation and a recorded baseline.

The changed citation is content/resources/provider-workflows/cross-provider-evaluation-migration-workflow.json. It was an unregistered publisher record and had never been verified, so it has been removed from the source list and replaced with the cited publications from the National Institute of Standards and Technology. The change affects the guide's provenance and support for its risk-management, measurement, and verification guidance. It does not change the migration procedure.
sections.callout: Do not claim that results are equivalent when the baseline, scoring method, or execution conditions cannot be reconstructed. Establish a new baseline and record the break in comparability instead.

sections.title: Migration playbook
paragraphs: Step 1: Freeze the evaluation intent before changing the implementation. Record the behavior being tested, representative test cases, instructions, scoring method, acceptance criteria, and the evidence retained from the source-provider run. If any element cannot be reconstructed, stop the direct comparison, label the old baseline as incomplete, and create a documented baseline that future runs can reproduce.

Step 2: Separate provider-neutral test content from provider-specific adaptations. Preserve the meaning and expected outcome of each test while recording any adaptation required to submit it to the destination provider. If an adaptation changes the task, available context, or expected response, classify that test as non-comparable and evaluate it separately rather than combining it with the comparable set.

Step 3: Define comparable run conditions before execution. Record the inputs, evaluation population, scoring process, repetition policy, and environmental conditions that could affect interpretation. If a condition cannot be matched, record the difference before running the evaluation and restrict conclusions to questions that the remaining evidence can answer.

Step 4: Run a small validation subset through the complete destination-provider workflow. Confirm that inputs arrive intact, outputs are captured, and the scoring process can evaluate them as intended. If the subset fails, correct the transport or scoring mismatch and repeat the subset; if correction would alter test intent, mark the affected cases non-comparable and do not proceed with an equivalence claim for them.

Step 5: Run the full comparable set and retain case-level evidence rather than only an aggregate result. Apply the documented scoring method consistently and route ambiguous cases through the previously defined review process. If evidence is missing or a score cannot be reproduced, rerun the affected case when permitted; otherwise exclude it from the comparison and record the exclusion and its effect on coverage.

Step 6: Compare results against the predeclared acceptance criteria and inspect individual regressions, not only the aggregate outcome. Approve migration only when the retained evidence supports the intended decision. If criteria are not met, investigate whether the cause is a destination-provider limitation, an invalid adaptation, or an evaluation defect; remediate the identified cause and rerun affected tests, or reject the migration if the cause cannot be resolved.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: The expected evidence is a migration record containing the frozen evaluation intent, the source baseline, documented adaptations, comparable and non-comparable case classifications, run conditions, case-level outputs, scores, exclusions, reviewed regressions, and the final decision against the stated acceptance criteria.

Verify success by selecting cases from the retained record and tracing each one from its original test intent through any adaptation, captured output, score, and final comparison. Confirm that every reported aggregate can be derived from included case-level results and that non-comparable or missing cases are disclosed. If a trace cannot be completed or an aggregate cannot be reproduced, treat verification as failed, correct the record or calculation, and repeat the check before relying on the migration decision.

Verify the scope of the conclusion separately. Confirm that the decision covers only the tested behaviors and documented conditions. If the conclusion extends beyond that evidence, narrow it to the supported scope or collect and evaluate the additional evidence before making the broader claim.
